The source establishes continued processing but does not expressly establish that substantive relief is unavailable. This interpretation remains unresolved, even where the formula faithfully implements the candidate's declared assumption.

A pending-at-commencement fact remains permanently true under these formulas. The source does not expressly establish permanent disqualification after a subsequent decision, withdrawal or resubmission.

The introductory immediate-effect language and the specific 28 November 2025 commencement provision should be reconciled. The specific date supports the proposed commencement assumption, but the source does not identify a universal assessment or implementation event for every transitional case.

The supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no descriptions connecting them to particular authorities. No catalogue match can be inferred. Relevant FAQs, existing-process rules and any necessary SFC clarification remain unavailable.

Home-jurisdiction compliance and the novel, complex and possible-local-policy classifications are supplied inputs, not implemented legal assessments. Applying these formulas to actual changes requires applicable home requirements and relevant interpretive guidance.
The circular's defined UCITS class includes the specified four EU domiciles and UK UCITS. No separate home-supervision eligibility condition follows expressly from the statement of purpose.
Removal of prior approval does not resolve notification, filing, post-vetting, overall compliance or the underlying approval obligation when removal is unavailable.
